title: Kernel Scribe Autotuner: seq-phase and chiplet-aware kernel selection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an online autotuner called Kernel Scribe that fingerprints each request and learns a lightweight mapping from architecture fingerprint, chiplet topology, sequence-phase histogram, and request priority to a recommended kernel implementation. Goal: reduce tail latency and token cost for mixed prefill/decode workloads while providing rollback safety and operator explainability.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel Scribe runs as a lightweight sidecar with median overhead <2ms on p4d and documented CPU cap
Learned policy improves mean decode latency by >=6% and 95th percentile by >=10% on mixed-chat benchmark vs static baseline
Safety guardrail: automatic fallback to safe-kernel on 3 consecutive regressions or if score confidence <0.15
Telemetry surfaced in Console: per-route kernel-choice, latency, cost delta, and A/B cohort tagging
Documented canary -> ramp deployment with automated rollback hooks
tasks: Design per-request fingerprint schema (arch ID, SM count, chiplet partitions, max_seq, seq-phase histogram)
Implement microbench runner for candidate kernels across seqlen buckets and chiplet configs
Prototype scoring model: logistic cost-composite with decay-weighted seq-phase matching
Integrate scoring sidecar into runtime probe path and add async telemetry emitter
Implement safe-fallback policy, health endpoints, and unit tests
Add Console widgets: kernel-choice heatmap and cost/latency deltas
Run 2-week shadow evaluation on Dedicated pools and analyze regressions
